items.title: Adds rebalance child-resource operations and expansion properties
items.summary: The supplied file/name group adds RebalanceJob as a ProxyResource child of AmlFilesystem, with template-defined read, asynchronous custom PATCH, asynchronous delete, and list-by-parent operations. It also adds optional expansion create/read input runRebalanceJob with default true and a read-only rebalanceJobId, plus a paged rebalance collection model. These additions activate in 2026-08-01; their version decorators support the features rather than constituting publication-only changes.

inferenceResults.rationale: The complete referenced hunk adds RebalanceJob.tsp from an empty baseline: a new @added(2026-08-01) proxy child model and interface containing read, custom asynchronous PATCH, asynchronous delete, and list-by-parent templates. The target REST facts place all four operations on newly added rebalanceJobs paths; PATCH accepts the new optional adminStatus model, rather than narrowing an old request. No existing SDK method, input/output member, client placement, or customization is edited by this hunk, and no existing public surface is removed or renamed. Thus the new declarations and their lifecycle templates do not establish an existing-caller incompatibility; this conclusion does not assume language-specific generated signatures.

items.title: Adds rebalance state and update models alongside documentation cleanup
items.summary: The models.tsp group adds version-gated rebalance properties, read-only status/progress/metric fields and an expansion ARM ID, an optional adminStatus PATCH model, and state/admin unions. The new provisioning-state union uses the shared ARM terminal states and @Azure.Core.lroStatus; operational job states remain separate. Existing identity, metric-aggregation, and import/export update declarations receive documentation/suppression cleanup, not member-contract changes. The grouping does not imply these edits form one business feature.

inferenceResults.rationale: The complete referenced hunk only adds the version-gated RebalanceJobPropertiesProvisioningState, RebalanceJobStatusType, and RebalanceJobAdminStatus unions. The first includes shared ARM terminal states and Creating/Updating/Deleting; the latter two include string and new named values. It neither removes a previously accepted wire value nor renames or changes the extensibility of an existing SDK enum/member. @Azure.Core.lroStatus decorates only the new provisioning union, with no supplied edit to an existing SDK method's polling or result contract. New-type addition, not a usage-number or type-name inference, supports no breaking candidate.

guidance.section: Properties That Are Never Directly Set by the User
guidance.excerpt: It is common to have properties that are calculated by the service or otherwise not directly set by the user, examples include timestamps, dates, values that are only set by specific actions (on/off, enabled/disabled, provisioningState). You want to make sure that these properties are marked so that they will appear in responses and not requests. this is done using the @visibility(Lifecycle.Read) decorator instance.
